concept.name: Realized capitalization
concept.definition: Realized capitalization (realized cap) values each coin at the price when it last moved on-chain, rather than at the current price — approximating the aggregate cost basis of the network and the value 'stored' in the asset.
concept.intuition: Instead of pricing every coin at today's quote, realized cap asks: what did the market actually pay for all these coins when they last changed hands?
concept.mechanics: For UTXO chains, realized cap = Σ (UTXO value × price at the time that UTXO was created); Coin Metrics extends the same idea to account-based chains using each account's last-movement date. Coins last moved cheap are re-priced upward when spent (raising realized cap), and vice versa; lost or ancient coins carry near-zero weight, unlike in market cap.
concept.formula: Realized Cap = Σ value_i × price_last_moved_i (over all UTXOs/accounts).
concept.failure_modes: Exchange internal shuffles and self-transfers re-price coins at current levels without economic change of hands, injecting noise; on account-based chains the 'last moved' convention is cruder than UTXO-level data.
concept.misconceptions: Realized cap is not 'real money invested' — it ignores off-chain purchases and approximates cost basis from on-chain movement only. A coin unmoved since 2009 counts at ~$0, which is a feature (discounts lost coins), not a data bug.
concept.example: Coin Metrics' worked example: accounts holding 100 coins last moved in 2010 ($0), 1,000 coins moved in 2016 ($10) and 500 coins moved in 2019 ($100) give a realized cap of $0 + $10,000 + $50,000 = $60,000 regardless of today's price.
